title: Filing and Fighting a Case in Bangladesh Without Travelling: Power of Attorney and Virtual Hearings
metaTitle: File or Defend a Case in Bangladesh from Abroad
metaDescription: Can you file or defend a court case in Bangladesh from abroad? Learn about Power of Attorney, vakalatnama, virtual hearings, when personal appearance is required and criminal bail issues.
keywords: file case in Bangladesh from abroad
appear in court by video Bangladesh
heroIntro: Court cases in Bangladesh can last years, and NRBs cannot fly back for every hearing. Fortunately, civil cases can largely be handled through an advocate, and virtual court technology now exists, but there are situations where personal presence is unavoidable, especially in criminal cases. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Cases from Abroad: Key Points
points: In civil cases you can sue and defend through an advocate (vakalatnama) and a Power of Attorney holder.
The Use of Information Technology by Courts Act allows virtual hearings and video evidence in many courts, at the court's discretion.
Criminal cases are different: for bail and trial the accused usually has to appear or surrender in court.
Time limits are strict: do not wait until your trip home to start.
Choose an advocate you can communicate with easily, and ask for regular written updates.

sections.content:
In civil suits, a party can appear by a recognised agent (Order 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908) or by an advocate. You sign a vakalatnama authorising the advocate and, if needed, a Power of Attorney for a family member to sign documents and receive notices (see PoA guide). For evidence, you may later need to testify in person or by video. Ask your advocate early when your testimony is likely.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

• Family Court cases (divorce, dower, maintenance, custody) can be filed and defended through an advocate and PoA.
  • Land suits (title, partition, injunction) usually proceed through the advocate; your presence is needed mainly for evidence.
  • Money recovery and contract suits likewise.

Since 2020, the law allows courts to hold hearings through video conferencing and to take evidence remotely in suitable cases. In practice, this depends on the court's technical facilities and the judge's discretion. Ask your advocate to apply for a video hearing or to examine you by commission. Prepare a stable internet connection, a quiet room and ID documents when the time comes.

In criminal cases, the accused generally has to appear before the court to apply for bail; a bail petition filed by an advocate for an absent accused is usually not accepted. If there is a warrant or case against you in Bangladesh, speak to an advocate before you travel. You may need to surrender and apply for bail at the right court. Complaints and FIRs can often be fought and quashed in the High Court Division through a writ or criminal miscellaneous case, which an advocate can file without your presence.

• Check enrolment and experience in the relevant court.
  • Agree fees and stages in writing, with receipts.
  • Insist on an update after every hearing, with copies of orders.
  • Give limited authority and avoid blank signed papers.
  • Appoint a trusted local contact to attend the court and collect documents.

1. Sign a vakalatnama and, where needed, a Power of Attorney attested at the Bangladesh Mission.
  2. Send scanned copies of all documents to the advocate.
  3. Keep a cause list and a calendar of hearing dates.
  4. Discuss strategy: injunction, mediation or settlement.
  5. Plan your travel only when your presence is truly needed.

faqs.question: Can I file a case in Bangladesh from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, in most civil matters through an advocate and Power of Attorney. Criminal cases are more restricted.

faqs.question: Can I attend court by video?
faqs.answer: The law allows virtual hearings and video evidence in many courts at the judge's discretion.

faqs.question: Do I have to travel for a criminal case?
faqs.answer: Usually the accused must appear for bail and trial, although some quashing proceedings can be filed through an advocate.

faqs.question: What is a vakalatnama?
faqs.answer: A signed authority by which a client appoints an advocate to act in a case.

faqs.question: How can I track my case from abroad?
faqs.answer: Ask your advocate for hearing updates and copies of orders, and use the court's online case search where available.
